launches.title: Twolabs - Humanoid robots for caregiving
launches.tagline: Socially intelligent humanoids to assist the elderly.
launches.body:
**TL;DR -**

[Twolabs](https://www.twolabs.ai/) builds humanoid robots for caregiving.

Our robots will assist at nursing homes and senior living centers to take care of the elderly, starting with feeding, dressing, medication, daily tasks, and companionship.

We have our first robot design Tobi, are actively training VLAs, and building the social intelligence layer. Check out our [launch video](https://youtu.be/70T6AzTqIHc?si=CwZwf999yWGGNFk3).

**What we do**

Twolabs builds semi-humanoid robots for nursing homes and senior living communities. We're building the robot to achieve the following goals for the elderly:

* **Everyday help.** Feeding, dressing, medication reminders, fetching objects, the daily physical work of getting through a day.
* **Mobility support.** A stabilization aid so residents can walk safely, plus wayfinding around the facility.
* **Companionship.** Conversation, presence, real social support, so a resident isn't alone all day.

We build the full stack in-house, the robot hardware and all the AI that makes it socially capable. Most of robotics right now is chasing warehouse manipulation, moving boxes and folding laundry. We think the harder and more important problem is robots and people working closely together.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101964&key=user_uploads/2115411/ee3141ab-259b-402a-8ee5-5e10b8ce37fd)

**The backstory**

I'm [Sardor](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sardor-rahmatulloev). I was born in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, moved to the US at six, and studied CS at Cornell. At Cornell I led a 40+ engineer team building autonomous combat robots. We were ranked top 5% nationally; most of my team went on to defense tech and semiconductors. My faculty advisor was Professor Tapo Bhattacharjee, who runs one of the leading caregiving robotics labs in the country. After Cornell I joined Meta Superintelligence Labs at 23 years old, working on GPU optimization, foundation model training, and AI infra. I left to start Twolabs. (I also got to be the first Uzbek founder to get into YC.)

[Danyal Ahmad](https://www.linkedin.com/in/danyalahmad1/) is my co-founder, and we have known each other for over nine years, since high school. We interned together at Salesforce in 2024 and have built a lot of products together since. Danyal has an MS in AI from Georgia Tech, and fine-tuned video models at Salesforce.

We started Twolabs because our grandparents face a lot of health conditions as they grow older, and we wanted to build a robot that can assist them in their daily lives. The need is everywhere: the US is short hundreds of thousands of caregivers and the gap widens every year as the population ages. A caregiver costs a facility around $60K/year, turnover is brutal, and the work is physically and emotionally exhausting. Meanwhile the people who need help, getting out of bed, eating, not being alone all day, don't get enough of it. A robot doesn't replace caregivers. It takes the repetitive physical load off them so one caregiver can do more for more residents, and residents get help when they actually need it.

**Our bet**

Most robotics companies fall into one of two camps:

* **Task robots** that can do physical work but can't relate to a person.
* **Social robots** that can hold a conversation but can't actually do anything.

Each succeeds at one half of the problem. But we think a truly helpful robot has to handle both, completing the physical task and engaging with the person in front of it. Too many humanoids are optimizing for task completion alone. We're betting the robots that actually help people will need to be socially intelligent to do it.

The other half of our bet is how robots are built. Companies have to be vertically integrated to win in robotics right now. We build the hardware and the AI together, because at this stage of Physical AI the models need to be specific, not general-purpose.

**Where we are**

Prototype design completed and our AI stack in active development. We're advised by Professor Zackory Erickson at Carnegie Mellon, whose research is at the leading edge of assistive robotics.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101964&key=user_uploads/2115411/551aef43-2a9c-4786-831c-ea4c32f77551)

**Our asks**

1. **Engineers and research scientists.** If you or someone you know is proficient in VLA research, reinforcement learning, or robotics foundation models, we're hiring AI engineers and research scientists.
2. **Investors.** Investors in robotics, humanoids, healthcare, or hard tech, especially anyone who's been close to elder care.

Contact us directly at [sardor@twolabs.ai](mailto:sardor@twolabs.ai) and [danyal@twolabs.ai](mailto:danyal@twolabs.ai). And check out our website at [twolabs.ai](http://twolabs.ai).

launches.body:
Hub provides real-world training data to frontier AI labs and robotics companies. We went to 7-figure revenue agreement on data delivery during the last weeks, working with some of the biggest names in AI and robotics.\
\
**Why now**

The gap between frontier models is closing, and internet-scale data is largely exhausted. The only edge left is real-world data that humans have to produce. Every lab now wins or loses on its edge cases, and edge cases need specific data captured by specific people: data that doesn't exist anywhere online. Whoever can go collect the right data first ships the better model first. Human labor is half of global GDP, and almost none of it has been recorded yet.

**What Hub does**

We capture this data through a global network of humans, across all continents. We route and activate the exact people who fit a lab's brief and deliver in days, not the months it takes to source a generic dataset off the shelf. Because we collect the data ourselves, we can attest its provenance, which you can't do for data you didn't capture. Our ML and QA pipelines then verify and enrich it, so we meet the hardest dataset requirements labs throw at us. The moat isn't the data, it's how fast we can go get it.

**Traction**

From 5-figure to 7-figure in revenue agreement on successful data delivery. We now work with some of the biggest frontier AI labs and robotics companies in the world.

**The ask**

Two asks: —> You're building frontier models or robots and data is your constraint. \
—> You're a top robotics engineer, a PhD whose research touches robotics or egocentric data, or someone with deep experience at a leading robotics lab, we're hiring. \
\

launches.title: StableBrowse - Browser Layer For AI Agents
launches.tagline: We enable agents to navigate the web with 70% fewer tokens and 4x faster execution.
launches.body:
**TL;DR**: StableBrowse is the browser layer for AI agents. We transform dynamic websites into structured knowledge graphs that capture how sites truly work, giving agents persistent memory to complete tasks reliably without starting from scratch every time.

**Ask**: If you’re building agents that browse the web, scrape data, fill forms, monitor prices, or work inside authenticated portals, we’d love to talk! Reach us at [team@stablebrowse.ai](mailto:team@stablebrowse.ai) or schedule a demo at [stablebrowse.com](http://stablebrowse.com).

<https://youtu.be/ng_ZM1PCkv0?si=x4pVN9tEb5PNhfxv>

**Problem**: AI agents are increasingly being used for real web workflows like tracking competitor pricing, applying for loans, updating CRM records, booking travel, submitting expense reports, and navigating legacy enterprise systems.

Most browser agents still treat every interaction like it’s the first time, repeatedly asking an LLM what to click next. This works in demos, but breaks in production because websites constantly change through:

* Pop-ups and modal interruptions
* Login and authentication flows
* Slow-loading dropdowns and forms
* Layout and UI updates
* Dynamic page behavior

As a result, agents become unreliable, expensive to run, and difficult to scale across real-world workflows.

**Solution**: StableBrowse gives AI agents persistent memory of how websites actually work by converting websites into structured execution graphs. Instead of rediscovering workflows every run, StableBrowse learns websites once and reuses that knowledge across future executions.

We convert pages into structured states, turn buttons and forms into reliable actions, extract clean structured data instead of raw HTML, and detect when websites change to keep workflows reliable over time.

At runtime, StableBrowse handles:

* Navigating known workflows
* Filling forms and completing submissions
* Extracting clean, structured data
* Handling date pickers and dropdowns
* Detecting when websites change
* Returning usable outputs instead of raw HTML

This allows the LLM to focus on user intent instead of fragile browser interactions. The results are dramatic: 70–80% lower token usage, 3–4× faster workflows, and up to 98% success rate.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101987&key=user_uploads/1853933/3903c45b-f3a3-4e2d-84dd-f2bb28a9eaf2)

\
**Background**: We started StableBrowse after running into these same frustrations ourselves while building browser agents. Our team brings experience from Amazon (agentic commerce), AWS EC2 Nitro, applied AI research, and multiple fast-growing startups.

launches.title: Proprio Robotics - Autonomous Data Centers

launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106864&key=user_uploads/2910355/e9094f01-f5e9-4c30-93c6-81d8f041957d)

### **Physical AI for Data Centers**

Over the next five years, more than $7 trillion is projected to flow into data center buildout. But the supply chain is still heavily manual and fragmented, and can’t keep pace with current demand. **Proprio Robotics** is building autonomous robots for the entire data center lifecycle—assembly, maintenance, and decommissioning.

See our [launch video!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=999uFeKGyVY)

### **The Problem**

Building and running AI compute infrastructure requires dealing with delicate and fragile components that traditional automation simply cannot do. As a result, servers are manually assembled by hand overseas, and spend weeks in transit before they are integrated into racks and delivered to data centers. Once they get there, labor constraints exacerbate the issue of maintenance. Today, hundreds of thousands of technician positions go unfilled in the United States. Finally, when the servers are retired, there is no efficient way to extract valuable components inside like GPUs and memory.

### **What We're Building**

We develop physical AI models and custom hardware, purpose-made to give robots the dexterity and intelligence to perform various server-related manipulation tasks.

* **Assembly** **-** Autonomous robots can assemble servers onshore without driving up labor costs, supporting the growing need to bring ODMs back to the United States.
* **Maintenance** **-** We use the same technology for live data center maintenance. We built a working AI data center in our office, and our robot can actively maintain it 24/7. We’re deploying this technology to commercial data centers in the coming months.
* **Decommissioning** **-** Our robots also break down previous-generation servers and pull out reusable parts, and we're working with enterprise circular programs and IT Asset Disposition companies to return scarce components to circulation.

### **Why This Matters**

The immense demand for compute requires new innovation. 

To solve power and cooling constraints, operators are building data centers away from the grid, near nuclear facilities, on the water, and in space—environments where it’s not easy to staff humans. With autonomous data centers, we can take human ergonomics and labor constraints out of the picture and redesign entire facilities from scratch.                    

### **Who We Are**

We're graduate robotics researchers out of **Berkeley AI Research** and **Harvard AI and Robotics Lab**. Anirudh’s spent years working at one of the country's leading robotics labs, training dexterous manipulation models alongside NVIDIA's GR00T team. Raghav’s led research centered on reinforcement learning and humanoid world models. Both of us are extremely excited to bring this expertise to the AI compute industry, where robotic automation will be indispensable for meeting demand.

### **Our Ask**

As we advance our technology, we’d like to push for more commercial deployments. If you / anybody you know works in any stage of the AI compute lifecycle, we’d love to chat. Reach out to us at [founders@propriorobotics.com](mailto:founders@propriorobotics.com) :)

launches.title: Edgerun: The 10 lb Military Exoskeleton
launches.tagline: Powered exoskeleton that assists every step a soldier takes under combat load
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Edgerun builds powered legs for soldiers. A 10 lb exoskeleton worn at the waist that adds assistance to every step and cuts the effort of moving under a combat load by 30-45%. Since May, we've run 100+ field tests with Ukrainian operators out of our Kyiv field office.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nFLeQV2DWMc>

**▍The problem**

Every system on the modern battlefield has been upgraded. The human carrying it has not.

* For 2,500 years the soldier's load sat around 40 lbs. In the last 40 years it **doubled, then doubled again**.
* A US infantryman now carries **90-140 lbs** into a fight. The Army's own field manual sets the limit at 48 lbs.
* On deployment, load carriage causes **twice as many** evacuations as enemy contact.
* The Pentagon and VA spend **$9.3B a year** on the injuries it leaves behind.

Battles are won through speed and surprise. Load kills both.

**▍Why now**

Sixty years of military exoskeletons died the same death. The device cost more to carry than it gave back. SOCOM's TALOS burned $400M before it was cancelled in 2019.

That all changed in the last 18 months. The humanoid robotics boom produced one-pound actuators that put out 30+ Nm of torque, and 21700 cells crossed 450 Wh/kg. The components finally exist. They’re getting better every quarter.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/cd255b24-3429-4270-9670-e28fc8df360b)

**▍What we built**

Our first exoskeleton is a bilateral hip system worn at the waist. It reads your gait in real time and adds torque at the moment your hip drives forward. The hip produces about 60% of the force in loaded walking, so assisting it gives the most help-per-pound of anything you could strap to the body.

* Under 10 lbs with batteries
* 30-45% less metabolic cost under a combat load
* On in 5 seconds, off in one
* 12+ hours on hot-swappable drone-class batteries
* Quasi-direct-drive actuators, composite structures, CAN bus. Nothing exotic by design.

The soldier arrives at the objective still able to fight, patrols 10 km farther, and keeps a body that lasts past one tour.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/94bf48a9-0ba6-4ce7-94a2-f467cae9657c)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/883d1e98-900a-420a-b7ff-e56cc8911c0c)

**▍Ukraine**

Our field engineers work out of a Kyiv office, alongside operators from infantry, special operations, and National Guard units who provide structured feedback every day. [Balistyka](https://balistyka.ua/), one of Ukraine's leading body armor makers, is an integration partner, helping us ensure our system fits the kit soldiers already wear.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/89a30d39-fe11-421c-abe7-32961da8d1bd)

**▍The mission**

Defense is the first customer, not the last. Read the mission at edgerun.com/mission

🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110611&key=user_uploads/3652354/be41c9e5-378d-452f-a111-10380035f14d)

**Every electric motor runs on rare-earth magnets.** EVs, drones, robots, wind turbines, guided munitions: nearly all of them are dependent on Chinese magnets. On January 1st, 20270, [regulation changes will make it illegal to deliver anything that walks, drives, or flies to US Defense if it contains a magnet produced in covered countries like China.](https://www.massmagnetics.com/comply) The domestic supply chain meant to replace it doesn't exist yet. **Mines take a decade to permit, and the ore they pull up leaves radioactive tailings behind, making permitting magnet mining a nightmare.**

We’re[ ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/energyeric)the founders, [Eric Silver](https://x.com/metalscontent) and [Matthew Grol](https://www.linkedin.com/in/matthew-groll/)l (left and right in the pic below). We’ve known each other since grade school. Since then, Eric’s built multiple battery pilot production lines and materials science labs in the Midwest for NSF-funded companies. Matthew’s built exquisite aerospace gear including Moon-regolith melters and ultra-precise guidance systems for the world’s foremost labs at NASA, Draper, and MIT. **Together we’re making one bet: America's rare-earth problem isn't a mining problem.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110611&key=user_uploads/3652354/2046e9de-2db6-47e8-91fc-651e31e5a834)

**Mass Magnetics’ unfair advantage is sitting in end-of-life electric vehicles, hard drives, and industrial equipment.** The team uses AI models and robotics trained on real scrap to sort metallurgy by exact grade and chemistry. Then, a rapid-sintering process takes that reclaimed mass to a finished magnet in 3 minutes, where conventional approaches take over 4 hours. The result is a magnet as strong as anything imported, with no radioactive footprint or bureaucratic permitting, fully compliant for US defense.

**If you build robots, drones or motors visit our site and reach out at [outreach@massmagnetics.com](mailto:outreach@massmagnetics.com) and get your magnets.**

launches.title: Enact: post-training infrastructure for robotics models
launches.tagline: Enact generates the data and evaluations needed to make robotics models reliable in the real world.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Enact helps teams deploy robots that work in the real world. We roll out policies, generate failure / recovery data, and run in-house evaluations so robots can complete real tasks in production.** 

[**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dam0tQBIezY**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dam0tQBIezY)

**The Problem**

Robotics models can look flawless in choreographed demos and still fail when an object slips, the scene shifts, or the robot makes an early mistake. Those failures push the policy into states its training data never taught it to recover from. **Robotics models must train on edge cases to be reliable in the real world.**

**What We Built**

Enact turns a policy’s failures into targeted recovery datasets for teams training robotics models. We use the data to fine-tune models and run real-world evaluations, verifying our data improves reliability.

**We’re already serving our first customers: finding where their robots fail and collecting the targeted recovery data needed to make them robust.**

* Roll out an existing model on a physical robot.
* Identify recurring failure states.
* Recreate those states and demonstrate how to recover.
* Retrain with the new trajectories added in.
* Repeat

**Targeted recovery data pushes success rates above 99%.**

On our controlled packing task using pi0.5 on the YAM 6DoF arms:

* 200 ordinary expert demonstrations: 90/100 successful physical rollouts
* 250 ordinary expert demonstrations (more of the same data): 89/100
* 200 expert demonstrations plus 50 targeted recovery demonstrations: 99/100

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109880&key=user_uploads/2406199/e1b83c19-6e1d-4dda-adcf-258398bc1676)

**We’re continuing to longer-horizon tasks such as industrial kitting, lab automation, and electronics recycling**

Longer-horizon tasks need substantially more base and recovery data, but the loop is the same: find failures, target missing behaviors, retrain, repeat.

**Who We Are**

We’re James Stevens and Govind Chada, and we met at Stanford. Govind researched real-world robot adaptation in Chelsea Finn’s IRIS Lab and co-developed recovery methods published at top robotics conferences. Together, we built Enact’s in-house data and evaluation operation and are already serving robotics teams. We started Enact to make robotics models work reliably outside the lab.

**Our Ask**

Training a robot foundation model or deploying a policy that fails on a real task? Tell us the model, task, and where it breaks, and we’ll make it work.

Email: [founders@enact.company](mailto:founders@enact.company)

launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/oHKXAeiH79Y>

**TLDR:** Synapse Semiconductor builds image sensors that process **AI on the sensor** itself. Each pixel captures light and runs neural-network computation in the same device, replacing the need for a GPU while cutting the power and latency of edge vision.\
\
\
A camera has no use by itself. Its value is only when its information gets evaluated. How can a camera that only has value when combined with a GPU support local intelligence? GPUs will get better, yet the fundamental problem is the separation of the camera and the GPU. Solving that separation will unlock bountiful innovation in machine perception. 

**RETINA: a chip designed like the human retina which runs neural network operations in the camera pixel.** 

\
We have compressed the whole edge AI vision hardware stack into **one wafer**. CNNS, VLMS, etc can run on just one chip that senses light. Our compute transistors are also the same photosensors that see light. There is no longer separation between compute (Nvidia Jetson Nano) and a camera (RealSense Depth Camera). \
\
If you are building robotic perception, drones, and vision systems for physical AI —> [book.synapsesemi.org](http://book.synapsesemi.org)

name: DeepReach Inc.
long_description:
Physical AI — robots and world models — is bottlenecked on one thing: diverse,
real-world data at massive scale showing how humans actually do work in the
physical world. It was never written down, and you can't buy it, because no one
has ever captured it. Only real local experts, the people who do this work every
day, can produce data this authentic and valuable.

DeepReach builds the network that reaches them. We design and manufacture
wearable stereo capture devices, then place them with local data partners who
run collection as their own business — in warehouses, workshops, farms, kitchens
and repair shops. They own the local relationships; we supply the hardware, the
software platform, the quality pipeline and the payments. Anyone can run a data
business.

That structure is what produces diversity. Instead of thousands of hours inside
one environment, we deliver hours spread across thousands of environments —
which is what actually makes robot policies generalize.

475 devices in the field and 100+ data partners are live across 7 countries, adding new
partners every week. They've collected nearly 150,000 clips in the past three
months, with volume roughly doubling month over month. Our data is in production
with multiple frontier model and robotics companies, and we're scaling to
10,000+ devices across 50 countries.
one_liner: Network for Physical AI Data Business

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
Chris and I are from the same hometown and have known each other for ten years, long before either of us thought about robots.

In that time I built two companies around the same problem: how do you organize people you'll never meet, in places you'll never visit, to do consistent work? The first was HireIO, a cross-border staffing platform out of Silicon Valley. The second was Talex, an expert network for LLM data annotation — around 70,000 people across ten countries. Chris went the other direction: a CS PhD at USC in computer vision, ML infrastructure at Meta, then founding ML engineer at Aven.

Running an annotation network for language models, I kept hitting the same wall from the supply side. Text was running out, and the next generation of models wasn't going to learn from the internet. It was going to learn from the physical world — and nobody had captured it. What a warehouse picker, a line cook or a phone repair technician knows is real expertise, and none of it was ever written down. You can't buy that data, because it doesn't exist yet. Chris was hitting the same wall from the model side, watching what was missing from training sets.

The default answer at the time was to put a lab in one city and record thousands of hours in the same room. That produces volume, not diversity, and robot policies don't generalize from volume. What the models needed was the opposite shape: a few hours each from thousands of different real workplaces, all over the world. Which meant the bottleneck wasn't an AI problem. It was a distributed human network problem — reaching thousands of ordinary businesses across dozens of countries, and giving the people already working in them a reason to capture what they do. That was the problem I'd spent two companies learning to solve.

We started DeepReach in 2025. Chris owns perception and the data engine; I own the network, hardware operations and the commercial side. Ten years of knowing each other means we skipped most of the negotiation that takes co-founders their first year.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Core problem: robot models can't generalize, because the data they learn from all looks the same.

Physical AI needs to see how work actually happens — a mechanic torquing a bolt, a baker shaping dough, a technician opening a phone. None of it was ever written down. The internet captured what people say about the world; it never captured how people act in it. So unlike language models, this generation can't be trained on scraped text. Every hour has to be collected on purpose. 

Today the field has roughly tens of thousands of hours of this data against a need estimated in the hundreds of millions. But the gap isn't really a volume gap. It's a diversity gap. The standard approach is to build a lab, hire operators, and record for months in one controlled space. That yields thousands of hours that all look alike, and a policy trained on it fails the moment the lighting, the counter height, or the tool changes. Our customers' acceptance specs now reflect this directly: they cap how much of a delivery can come from any single environment type, and reject batches that are too concentrated. Diversity is the binding constraint, and it's now contractual.

Diversity is hard for an economic reason, not a technical one. Collecting one hour each from a thousand real workplaces means negotiating access to a thousand real businesses — each with an owner who has no reason to let a stranger film their operation, in a country where you have no presence. That cost is why everyone else builds the lab instead. It's a distribution problem wearing an AI problem's clothes. \
\
That's why we built the company as a network rather than an operation. The people who already work in those places, and already have the trust and the access, run collection as their own local business. We give them the hardware, the software and the payments. Access stops being something we buy and becomes something the network already has. \
\
I decided to work on this from the supply side. I'd spent two companies building cross-border human networks — a staffing platform, then a 70,000-person annotation network across ten countries — and kept watching demand arrive for data that no existing structure could produce. The bottleneck was never the model. It was that nobody had built the network that reaches the physical world.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
The long-term vision is a network that can reach any workplace on earth, and a record of how human work is actually done.

Concretely: 10,000+ devices, 50 countries, one million commercial scenes, ten million task types. Every deployment adds to what we call the Human Skill Library — a permanent record of how people do physical work, built from the inside by the people who do it. Much of this knowledge exists nowhere else. It lives in the hands of a mechanic who has been doing the job for thirty years, and when he retires it's gone. Text and video on the internet captured what people say about work. Nobody has captured the work. 

\
If we succeed, two things are different：\
First, robots stop being confined to the places that can afford to build around them. Today automation only pays at Amazon scale — a facility large enough to redesign itself for the machine. That's a rounding error of the world's actual workplaces. A policy trained on a million real environments doesn't need the environment to change; it works in a repair shop with bad lighting and a counter at the wrong height. That's the difference between robotics as a capability the largest companies buy and robotics as infrastructure a small business can use.\
Second, the people whose work teaches these models are inside the economy that results. The last generation of AI was trained on data scraped from people who were never asked and never paid. This one has to be collected on purpose, from real workers in real workplaces, which means it can be built the other way — as something people opt into and earn from. We already have data partners in ten countries running this as a business they own. At 10,000 operators that isn't a side effect of how we source data. It's the point.

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** DeepReach is a global data network that equips local entrepreneurs with wearable devices to capture the real-world operation data for Physical AI training. By decentralizing collections across thousands of entrepreneurs who have access to local businesses, they provide high-diversity training data that cannot be accessed elsewhere. DeepReach already signed multiple-million-dollar contracts with frontier AI labs.\
\
**DeepReach is building a global network for real-world human data to train Physical AI.**

We enable local entrepreneurs to operate data-collection businesses using our wearable capture devices, while we provide the hardware, software, QA, and customers.

The result is a distributed network that produces the diverse human demonstrations Physical AI labs cannot obtain anywhere else. Every new data partner expands the diversity and value of the network.

In just three months, DeepReach has helped **150+ entrepreneurs** build data businesses employing **1,000+ local experts** across **7 countries**. Together, they’ve collected **500,000+ real-world operation clips**, captured **150,000+ professional skill demonstrations**, and secured **several million dollars in customer contracts** with frontier AI labs and robotics companies.

▶ **Watch how it works:** <https://youtu.be/q5mLwju5Q8U?si=CT3FHbNJaIteNXZD>

---

# **The Problem**

Frontier AI is already learning from the physical world.

The challenge is no longer collecting data, it’s collecting **diverse** real-world data at scale.

Most companies solve this by building collection labs or hiring workers directly. Both approaches scale headcount, but neither scales access. The hardest part is reaching millions of real workplaces across different industries, countries, and working conditions.

Without that diversity, AI struggles to generalize beyond a small number of controlled environments.

---

# **What We Built**

Instead of building another data collection company, **we built a platform where entrepreneurs launch independent real-world data businesses.**

DeepReach provides the wearable devices, software platform, quality infrastructure, customer demand, operational support, and payments. **Entrepreneurs build and grow the businesses.**

They recruit local experts, develop trusted relationships with local businesses, and continuously expand into new industries, communities, and real-world environments.

**Every new business expands the platform’s reach into the physical world, creating access to places, people, and skills that centralized data collection simply can’t reach.**

The result isn’t a larger workforce, it’s **a growing ecosystem of independent data businesses** that continuously expands the world’s supply of diverse real-world data for Physical AI.

---

# **Where We Are**

In just three months:

* **150+ entrepreneurs** have launched data businesses on DeepReach
* Those businesses now employ **1,000+ local experts** across **7 countries**
* **500,000+ real-world operation clips** collected
* **150,000+ professional skill demonstrations** captured
* **Several million dollars in signed customer contracts** with frontier AI labs and robotics companies
* Scaling toward **10,000+ devices** across **20 countries**

# **Where This Goes**

Our model is simple: labs list the tasks and environments they need, our entrepreneurs pick up the orders and go record them, and every delivery makes the network more capable of fulfilling the next one. It also compounds into something bigger, what we call the **Human Skill Library**: a growing record of how people interact with the physical world.

Most of this knowledge has never been documented. It lives in the hands of experienced workers, passed down through practice rather than words, and it often disappears when they retire.

Our vision is to preserve and scale humanity's physical knowledge, so every AI system can learn from the collective experience of human work.

# **About Us**

\
Tim built HireIO into a leading global workforce company with 15 millions in annual revenue, then founded [Talex.ai](http://Talex.ai), an AI-powered expert network, before starting DeepReach. Chris comes from a computer vision background. We discovered the problem firsthand while labeling data for robotics startups: the real bottleneck wasn’t annotation, it was capturing diverse real-world human skills at scale.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110389&key=user_uploads/1294315/9bb8c293-ab57-42aa-b756-58562e546b78)

---

# **How You Can Help**

If you’re building frontier AI systems and need more diverse real-world data, we’d love to talk.

If you’re an entrepreneur interested in building a real-world data business, applications are open here: [www.deepreach.ai/join](https://www.deepreach.ai/join)

Tim Li\
Founder & CEO, DeepReach AI

launches.title: Agency Tool Company: The build and deployment platform for robotics
launches.tagline: Field Robots Faster with ATC Deploy
launches.body:
Today we're sharing Agency Tool Company and our first product, ATC Deploy: a faster, more reliable way to ship software to robots wherever they are. It moves updates up to 20 times faster than docker pull or scp and works with any software stack already in use.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jx0rLRVa06s>

## The updates that took until 2 a.m.

Davis and I spent eight years building Scythe Robotics and putting hundreds of autonomous mowers to work across the country. For years, we deployed software with a tool I'd cobbled together for our first few robots. As the fleet grew, deployment became an ordeal: engineers stayed up until 2 a.m., we coordinated with customers to move robots out of sheds and into LTE coverage at set times, and failed transfers restarted from zero. Shipping a fix could take more coordination than building it. We had models to train and customers to serve, so the tooling limped along with incremental bandaids.

We've since heard the same story from robotics teams across industries. That deployment becomes a hidden bottleneck: teams become release-averse, feedback loops slow and improvements stall. Stitched-together web and IoT tools barely work if you know which scripts to run and who to call, so they survive, even if it means every update is distracting from improving the product.

## What we built

ATC Deploy ships whatever you already run: OS images, Docker images, or any file tree. Run “atc ota push user@robot”, and it sends only the changed bytes, then restarts your software through hooks you define—way faster than a docker push.

Install takes one “curl | sh” command and a config file so you can get back to work fast. Interrupted transfers resume where they stopped, and an offline robot can receive updates by USB if you need. There's no new runtime, packaging format, or operating system to adopt.

## Shipping to robots today

ATC Deploy already ships software to robots at Burro, which has deployed more than 750 machines worldwide, Tempo, polishing concrete across several US states and Canada, and Gather, who is scaling their 99.9% accurate inventory drones nationwide. Their teams spend less time managing delivery and more time improving the robot.

**Operate a robot fleet? Join the ATC Deploy waitlist at [agencytool.com](https://agencytool.com/).** Know a team that should be using it? Send them this post, or to [mailbox@agencytool.com](mailto:mailbox@agencytool.com).

It's time to build robots.

launches.tagline: Giving Robots Touch
launches.body:
6thSense builds wearable tactile sensing rigs that capture how human hands interact with the world — pressure, contact, grip, and pose — across touch, vision, depth, force, and 3D hand pose, all in real environments. We sell that multimodal data to the companies training the next generation of dexterous robots.\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gXx53tcIv5U>

Robots are getting good at seeing. They're still terrible at touching. That's because there's almost no data capturing what a hand actually feels while doing real tasks in real homes. Lab data doesn't cut it. We go anywhere and capture the missing layer that manipulation models need to learn fine motor control.

What makes our data different is the hardware we built to collect it. Our tactile sensing devices are designed and manufactured in-house, purpose-built to capture the richest touch signal in the industry — with scale in mind from the very beginning, enabling us to actually solve the tactile data problem. Every sensor maps directly to how robotic skin needs to work: a 1-to-1 analog for the tactile arrays going into the next generation of robot hands. That means the data we collect today doesn't just train better policies. It transfers directly to the hardware it's meant to run on. The team comes from Tesla, Mecka, Samsung, DoorDash, and Amazon, with expertise across hardware, sensors, ML, robotics, and software at scale. If you're training a manipulation policy or need custom tactile data, reach out.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Robots are finally capable enough to be useful, but they're priced like cars, not appliances. A capable humanoid costs $20,000+, so general-purpose robots stay in labs and pilots instead of homes. 

It's a big problem because household labor is one of the largest unpriced markets in the world. Today's answer is a stack of single-task machines, a dishwasher, a washer, a vacuum, each $600 to $1,000 and doing exactly one thing. Whoever ships a general-purpose robot at appliance prices doesn't win a niche, they open consumer robotics the way the PC opened computing.

We're robotics researchers from Columbia (RoboPIL, CGUI). After years watching \[$100K research robots struggle with tasks cheap hardware could handle\], we realized the gap between lab robots and home robots isn't intelligence, it's cost discipline. Nobody was going to fix that from inside a lab, so we left to build it: a $1,688 robot anyone can teach.

launches.title: Neuromorphic - Building an embodiment-agnostic “brain” that makes robots fast to deploy
launches.tagline: We make robots smarter, and faster to deploy. Starting with wet labs!
launches.body:
Hi everyone! We’re Cem, Ege, and Vatan, the founders of Neuromorphic 👋\
\
**TL;DR** Neuromorphic is building an embodiment-agnostic “brain” that makes robots fast to deploy, and easy to manage through natural interfaces like Slack, email, and phone. Our goal is to make deploying robots in wet labs and other physical industries as easy as onboarding a new employee.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6T0BDyjakmo>\
\
**The Problem**\
To make robotics mainstream, we believe two problems have to be resolved:\
1\. Deployment: Robots are still too slow, expensive, and engineering-intensive to deploy and adapt to new tasks and environments.\
2\. Interaction: Managing and controlling robots remains too technical.\
\
**What We’ve Built**\
Neuromorphic packages sensors, compute, and software into a “brain” that can be attached to any robot body. An onboard LLM orchestrator turns natural-language instructions into workflows made up of reusable robotic skills, such as navigating, picking up an object, opening a refrigerator, or inspecting an area. Individual skills can be of various types; they could be AI models we develop, like Vision-Language Models and Video Action Models, or just plain code. Sensor-based safety loops monitor every action to ensure reliable execution.

We are also giving robots emails, phone numbers, and Slack access to make human-robot interaction more intuitive than using dashboards. The robots then respond to queries and take actions using the onboard LLM.\
\
**Traction**\
Within a week of our first conversation with a leading biotechnology company, we deployed our robot in their wet lab, which is capable of operating autonomously 24/7, and already completed over 1500 tasks.\
\
**The Team**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109550&key=user_uploads/3607343/b28b023b-f328-4c5d-9181-720e96e5b1a3)

\
Cem: Second-time founder and did robotics research at Cambridge University. Previously built LLM routing and training acceleration, and did precision robotics.\
\
Vatan: Maintained multiple open-source robotics libraries, most notably MoveIt, one of the most popular motion-planning frameworks for robotics. Led various teams in robotics startups from Series A to Series C in Japan and Singapore. Deployed over a thousand robots.\
\
Ege: Did Robotics and AI research at Bilkent University. Research fellow at Nanyang Technological University. Published research in top AI and robotics conferences. Won HackMIT in 2024.\
\
Cem and Ege first met as teammates in the FIRST Robotics Competition. They reached out to Vatan for mentorship and robotics advice. We spent the next three years building robots and winning competitions together. We remained close and eventually reunited to start Neuromorphic!\
\
**Ask**\
We're looking for warm intros to wet lab, biotech, and physical-industry operators. If you have a repetitive physical process and have wondered whether a robot could do it, email us at [founders@neuromorphic.vision](mailto:founders@neuromorphic.vision) or [book a call here](https://cal.com/team/neuromorphic/meet-the-founders-of-neuromorphic).

name: Ultrasonium
long_description:
The technologies that define this century, including data centers, rockets, satellites, and robots, are built from complex metal parts. As these systems advance, the parts get harder to make. Past a certain complexity, casting and machining stop working, and the advanced methods that remain are slow, expensive, and hazardous.

Ultrasonium has invented a new manufacturing method to make these critical parts 15x faster and 75% cheaper than the methods they replace, in the U.S. and at scale. Solid metal feedstock goes in and a finished part safely comes out, controlled by a physical AI layer and novel control processes. 

The systems that matter most, in aerospace, energy, and compute, are demanding metal geometries that can't be machined or cast and are too expensive and slow to make with incumbent methods, at a moment when domestic manufacturing capacity is a national priority.

Our founding team has built and innovated some of the most complex engineering systems known to man: quantum computers, superconductors, nuclear reactors, and novel aerospace alloy processing methods.

launches.body:
**Building the toughest super computers for earth and space**\
\
**TL;DR:** Data centers are stuck for years waiting for power, while delayed construction sites across the world sit on unused interconnects, losing $1B per week in the US alone, in interest on trillions of dollars of debt. Our pods deploy on those sites and generate revenue for them in days. They use diamond wafers in the cooling system so pods run anywhere on earth, even a desert.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rf8cCV6qFow>

**The deal**

If you need compute (GPU hours, tokens, capacity for a training run) send us a note. We sell short and long-term contracts below market rate.

If your data has to stay on-prem (**defense, CUI, CMMC)**, we sell managed, modular pods directly and are already working with large aerospace companies.

**We're building factories**

SpaceX didn't just build rockets, they built rocket factories. We do the same and our first factory stands up over the next few months, potentially funded by the state of Missouri. We vertically integrate the critical components that currently carry multi-year lead times: transformers, switchgear and power distribution, and by taking control of our own supply chain we ensure we can build pods fast enough.

**Financed like aircraft**

Our pods are financed like aircraft - debt at **\~5-6%, not 11-15%**. A data center is a risky construction loan: money stuck in a half-built site for years, and if it fails the lender holds a building and a pile of GPUs priced by a brutally volatile market - the banks are freaking out. Our pods leave the factory fully functional, earns the moment it's connected to power, and can be repossessed and redeployed: the profile of equipment finance, far faster and cheaper.

**Traction**

Today we have $95M in LOI’s for our hosted compute and a further $27M for direct sales of our pods. Our first two clusters go live in Missouri this month, followed by the first modular factory.

**Our asks**

* **Compute buyers and offtake.** We'd love to speak to anyone buying compute, or setting up on-prem deployments, or needing CMMC compliance. Introductions to procurement teams at OpenAI, Anthropic, or any startup constrained by access to cheap compute would be incredible.
* **Hiring.** Data center engineers, electrical engineers, any data center nerds you know.
* **Financiers.** These projects run on capital from infra investors and tech lenders. If you've worked in that world, we'd love to chat.
* **Construction sites.** If you sell to construction sites, work in construction, mining, or fab production, or own a site yourself - we will put a money machine on it. Let's chat.

**Join us as we build supercomputers for the galaxy!**

launches.title: Cosmic Robotics: Autonomous construction on Earth and beyond
launches.tagline: Robotic construction equipment to build a city on Mars. We’re proving the technology by building large-scale infrastructure on Earth — utility-scale solar farms and hyperscale data centers.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We’re [James](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamesemerick/) and [Lewis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewis-c-jones/) - co-founders of [Cosmic Robotics](https://www.cosmicrobotics.com). 

**TL;DR**

**We build robotic construction equipment to build a city on Mars**. We’re proving the technology today by building large-scale infrastructure on Earth – utility-scale solar farms and hyperscale data centers. Our first machine, Cosmic-1, has already installed tens of thousands of solar panels in the field and more than doubled the productivity of traditional crews.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_Dl00xlJbcI> 

**❌ The problem**

After working at NASA JPL, SpaceX, and Relativity Space, we believe rockets are no longer the limiting factor to space exploration and that the first humans will land on Mars by 2034. **The new bottleneck is construction**. We won't be sending thousands of construction workers to Mars to build the energy, compute, and housing needed to sustain even a small city. **It has to be built by robots that don't exist yet**.

On Earth we have a similar problem - **we’ve lost the ability to build**. Construction productivity has declined for 50 years while manufacturing and agriculture became 10-15x more productive through automation. **The missing technology is robotic manipulation for the tasks still done by hand**: lifting, placing, fastening.

Meanwhile, there is a generational infrastructure buildout happening right now. **$7 trillion** is going into AI data centers, power, and compute over the next six years, **more than the Apollo Program, Manhattan Project, and Interstate Highway System combined**. 40% of US data center projects are running behind schedule, and the skilled labor shortage is the #1 cause. 

**🤖 What we've built**

Cosmic-1 is a 10,000 lb autonomous robot capable of heavy-lift manipulation. In solar, it picks up 90 lb panels and places them onto racking with millimeter precision in any environment: 100-degree heat, freezing rain, snow, and dust. It seamlessly integrates into existing construction processes. Across tens of thousands of cycles it has more than doubled the labor productivity of solar installation, on some of the largest solar projects in the US.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106899&key=user_uploads/522502/bb5f86ec-a23b-4ffd-a173-87f36ce6fb1c)

**👬 The Team**

We come at this problem from two angles. James (CEO) grew up on construction sites, then spent his career bringing robots to the field with Built Robotics and Autodesk Research. He learned you don't change the oldest industry in the world by disrupting it; you earn your way in by giving crews better tools.

Lewis' (CTO) life ambition is to build a city on Mars. His work at NASA, SpaceX, and Relativity Space spans rocket engines, launch vehicles, satellites, space stations, and, yes, Martian robots. When it became clear the space industry was well on its way to Mars, he went looking for the construction robots. When he didn't find them, we started Cosmic.

We’ve brought together a team of industry experts with experience building robots, rockets, drones, self-driving cars, humanoids, and nuclear reactor operations. We know what it takes to get a machine to show up day-in-day-out on the jobsite.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106899&key=user_uploads/522502/87f30a8e-6f83-490e-8bef-04225d1a525e)

**🚀 What's next**

We're scaling in solar, taking Cosmic-1 into data center construction, and working with NASA on lunar construction robotics. Revenue and data from deployments on Earth train the systems we'll deploy on Mars.

**🙏 Our asks**

1. **Know a hyperscaler or neocloud construction team?** Please connect us.
2. **Share this post** and [follow our journey](https://www.linkedin.com/company/cosmic-robotics/).

👉 Contact us at [james@cosmicrobotics.com](mailto:james@cosmicrobotics.com) | [cosmicrobotics.com](http://cosmicrobotics.com)

launches.title: Shiraz AI: Robots that learn on the job
launches.tagline: Deploy robots that learn new tasks from a single human demonstration in the factory
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We deploy robots that learn new tasks from a single human demonstration in the factory. A new task shows up on the floor? You just film it once on your phone and the robot picks it up. No sitting around collecting data. No engineer flying out to your site. No overnight fine-tuning. You show it, and the robot learns.

<https://youtu.be/OoQvOGrycDg>

**❌ The problem**

Manufacturing is full of constantly changing, high-mix production tasks, which are among the hardest to automate. A line that's packing one product today is building something completely different next week. Every factory owner we talk to says the same two things: they can't find enough people to do the work, and the automation solutions they've tried have been too expensive and too rigid, often ending up gathering dust in a corner.

**✅ What we do**

We're developing a robot foundation model whose core capability is adapting instantly to new variations of a task. You give the model a human demonstration video as context, and it bridges the embodiment gap to execute the task itself. This in-context learning is the missing piece in today's VLA approaches, and it's what changing manufacturing environments need.

We deliver the complete system: robot hardware, foundation model, and on-site deployment. We're already deploying robots at customer sites.

**👋 Who we are**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110367&key=user_uploads/585458/0832cd2d-2dfc-41b0-8de6-d29897b6c8d3)

Between the two of us, we have 20+ years of experience in robotics. Navid was part of the core team that productized Spot at Boston Dynamics and led manipulation projects there; before that, he was at Rethink Robotics. Mojtaba led whole-body control and bimanual manipulation efforts at Amazon Robotics and was a Research Assistant Professor at Northwestern University.

**🙏 Our ask**

Do you have a manufacturing task that needs automating, or know someone who does? Let us know and we'll automate it.

Reach us at: [founders@shiraz.ai](mailto:founders@shiraz.ai)

* We’re Brandon and Kingston, we've trained AI models for industrial cleaning robots and built production systems for camera fleets across the globe
* [**Brandon Ong**](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/388120)'s previous AI startup was backed by Sequoia. He did research on AI for low resource languages that topped Stanford’s LLM benchmark, SEA-HELM, and dropped out of his joint PhD in Robotics at Columbia and NTU

### **The Problem**

* **High quality data is the bottleneck for unlocking the next frontier of intelligence in robotics**
* Buyers want **data they can trust** 
* Data providers don’t have the bandwidth to provide signals and metrics about the quality of their data when they are **focused on** **operational excellence**

### **Our Solution**

* APIs for searching and analyzing Physical AI data at scale that enables providers to get **on-demand signals and metrics on data quality**
* Buyers demanding per-collector hour limits? **Prove compliance while we stay ahead of the workarounds**
* Changed standard operating procedures for collection? **Monitor for quality drift and regression**
* Suspect duplicate samples? **Verify quickly with a single API call**
* Our APIs enable **evaluation of data quality without training a robotics model, fast iteration cycles for** high quality data collection, and unlock **model improvements** 

### **How to reach us**

* We want to support data providers who believe in collecting high quality data in an ethical way
* To get started, email [**brandon.ong@hebbianrobotics.com**](mailto:brandon.ong@hebbianrobotics.com)

name: Robocurve
long_description:
Robocurve builds open-source tools and independent benchmarks to measure how well robots can do real-world jobs. Instead of relying on unverified demo videos from frontier labs, we score their models on reproducible benchmarks that anyone can trust.

Today there are no well-run, standardized robotics benchmarks. Labs evaluate in-house, and no independent group has stepped in to run continuous benchmarking as a service. The result is that no one actually knows how good anyone else is, or where the real frontier sits.

Good benchmarks require operating and maintaining physical hardware and real-world setups. Simulation only goes so far, since models that look strong in sim can show large performance gaps once deployed in the real world. Building real-world benchmarks means coordinating job-domain experts, evals engineering, and hands-on robotics all at once.

Frontier labs are targeting general-purpose robotics by 2028, yet the field of robotics evals barely exists. Whoever builds the trusted measure of robot capability becomes the reference everyone relies on. We combine backgrounds in AI evals and robotics to build and grow this field as fast as possible. We already shipped v1 of our open-source framework, Inspect Robots, and ran our first pilot scoring a frontier model on a real robot.
one_liner: Evals for robots

launches.title: Robocurve — Real-World Evaluations of Physical AI
launches.tagline: Real-world evals for robots
launches.body:
Hi, I’m [Jay](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeqcho/), co-founder of [Robocurve](http://robocurve.org). We measure and reports what frontier robots can actually do in the real world.

Our launch video <https://youtu.be/Cjkt2ikvsiQ>

Frontier labs are racing to build general-purpose robots within two years, yet no one knows what today's robots are truly capable of. Demo videos of robots performing narrow, cherry-picked tasks proliferate, but there are no rigorous, continuous, standardized benchmarks for robotics.

Robocurve builds benchmarks for robots and the AI models that control them, to help the world understand how far robotics has come and how fast it's moving. Our benchmarks range from playing Jenga and making a sandwich to constructing a data center.

General-purpose robots could arrive before the end of the decade, with far-reaching implications: accelerated data center buildouts, explosive economic growth from a fully automated economy, and intensified geopolitical competition between the US and China. Real-world evaluations from Robocurve will help clarify the timeline to general-purpose robots so that society can prepare for their arrival well ahead of time.

[Jay](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeqcho/) is a Rhodes Scholar and a top contributor to UK AI Security Institute's Inspect Evals. He has published papers in ICML, EMNLP, ACL, ACM EC and his research has been featured in MIT Technology Review. Previously, he spent time at AWS Bedrock, MATS, and Harvard where he completed his BA and MA with a highest honors thesis on AI and democracy.

If you build robots or AI models, reach out! We'd love to put them to the test. Learn more at [robocurve.org](http://robocurve.org).

launches.title: Salem Robotics - Autonomous robots for hazardous spaces
launches.tagline: We deploy robots to perform autonomous inspections and surveys in hazardous spaces, like nuclear.
launches.body:
We're [Caleb](https://www.linkedin.com/in/caleb-horan) and [Janak](https://www.linkedin.com/in/janak-panthi), PhD roboticists from UT Austin. We've spent a combined 15 years in nuclear, 10 of which deploying autonomous robots at Los Alamos National Lab, and we're building Salem Robotics.\
**TLDR:** Our software turns robots into independent survey and inspection workers at your facility.

[Launch Video](https://youtu.be/7xObOE6knZM)

## **Life and death pain worth $Millions/year**

At every nuclear facility, highly trained radiation-protection teams spend hours each day walking the site, filling out hand-drawn maps, and searching for something life-threatening: radiation. IN THE BEST CASE they find nothing, and still have to return to their posts to transcribe the data into a computer before doing the actual high-value work they were assigned. These surveys are time-consuming, dangerous, expensive, and prone to data inconsistencies that carry direct regulatory consequences.

The same pain exists well beyond nuclear. Whether it's gas-leak inspection or ammonia surveys, similar workflows run across oil, gas, chemical, biological, space, and other hazardous facilities.

## **What we do**

An operator defines the work from a simple dashboard; the robot then navigates the site, handles instruments, opens doors, turns valves, collects measurements, and generates structured, auditable, compliance-ready reports. We're hardware-agnostic, so plants run our software on robots they already own, many of which sit in a closet today as "$200k paperweights, " or we can provide the right robot for the job. Our stack is designed for safety-critical infrastructure and comes with theoretical safety guarantees, exactly what regulators and plant leadership require. Our core manipulation framework was not possible before and is based on **breakthrough founder research** published and presented at the most prestigious IEEE journals and conferences in the world. 

We're already in active contract-scoping conversations across the nuclear industry and oil & gas.

**Our asks**

* Intros to operations or innovation leaders in nuclear or similar hazardous sites (oil, gas, chem, bio, space).
* Advice from founders who've sold into safety-critical industrial environments.
* Sites where routine surveys are frequent, hard to staff, or particularly painful? We'd love to hear about them.

Comments, Emails, and DMs welcome. \

launches.title: Osseus: The intelligent development platform for robotics
launches.tagline: Build robots at the speed of software. Trace and fix all the downstream impacts of a design change.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Osseus plugs into the tools a robotics team already uses and crafts a live dependency graph of the entire robot. When you change a part, our agents trace what it affects across mechanical, electrical, and software, re-run the tests and sims, and then propose fixes in a branch for engineers to merge in.

**Ask:** If you work in robotics, as a professional or hobbyist, please reach out. Details at the bottom, or find us at [founders@osseus.ai](mailto:founders@osseus.ai).

<https://youtu.be/tEpkmA42fSA>

Hey everyone, we’re Anish and Ayush from Osseus. We’re building the intelligent development platform for robotics.

The age of robots is coming, and will not be unlocked by better AI models alone. Robot development is still messy and broken: every iteration crosses mechanical, electrical, software, suppliers, and testing, while the reasoning is scattered across tools and people. We’re building Osseus to make robot development agentic, compress the iteration cycle, and drive the avoidable cost of each design change to zero.

**The problem: One component change can break an entire robot build. A requirements error discovered during integration and testing can cost up to 78x more to fix than one caught upfront.**

Imagine the specified drive motor has a months-long lead time, or is underpowered, so the team selects a replacement. It looks similar, but it has a longer housing, draws more current, uses a different connector, and reports motion differently.

To the mechanical team, it is a motor swap. To electrical, it is a current and connector change. To software, it is a calibration change. The bracket, wiring, motor controller, thermal limits, firmware, requirements, and tests may all need review, but that chain is scattered across different tools and teams. Nobody sees the whole robot until integration fails.

**What we do: Trace the change, prepare the fixes, and validate them before the build.**

* **Build the requirements graph.** Osseus connects into the tools a robotics team already uses (CAD, ECAD, GitHub, Jira, docs, test runs) and crafts a live dependency graph of the entire robot. The extracted requirements are related to every component, decision, test and evidence that proves it.
* **Trace downstream impact.** When a change is made or being proposed, Osseus identifies the affected hardware, software, requirements, owners, tests, and simulations.
* **Run CI/CD across hardware and software.** Osseus' agents find which requirements may be compromised, run the attached tests and sims, create fixes for the affected hardware/software on branches, and re-run the tests to confirm the new design doesn’t break downstream.  Engineers see the proposed changes and evidence before approving and merging them.

**Design with parts you can actually get.**

The Osseus Marketplace brings nearby component availability and lead times into the design process. If the specified motor is unavailable, teams can find compatible alternatives to buy or rent and compare their effects on geometry, power, thermal limits, software, and testing before committing.

This helps builders keep prototypes moving instead of waiting weeks for parts. Teams and individuals can also monetize spare components and unused prototyping hardware by listing them for sale or rent.

**Design review that remembers.**

Engineers can see why a component was chosen, what was tried previously, and why an earlier design failed. Suppliers can comment directly on a part through a secure link. If a supplier flags that something cannot be manufactured or suggests a change that reduces cost, that insight stays connected to the design and resurfaces when relevant.

**The team**

We’re Imperial College London engineering and computer science graduates. Between us, we’ve done robotics research at Imperial, ML research at a Harvard-HKU lab, and built agentic systems at Apple.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109975&key=user_uploads/1409413/c2262c87-4d8b-4f68-a69d-3ec56d3eb217)

**How you can help**

We would love to speak with, or intros to:

* VPs and Heads of Engineering, Robotics, Systems, or Hardware at companies building physical robots.
* Robotic engineers who have felt the pain of integration.
* Hobbyists, university teams, and independent builders who build or modify robots.
* Anyone who has spare components they would list, or are looking to buy/rent.

We’re onboarding in waves - sign up to the [waitlist here](https://osseus.ai/)! Email us at [hello@osseus.ai](mailto:hello@osseus.ai) or[ book a call](https://osseus.cal.com/founders/osseus-intro).

launches.title: Dreamscale Labs: Running robot brains in the cloud
launches.tagline: The fastest cloud inference platform for robotics.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: We're 40-50% faster than existing cloud providers in serving frontier robot AI models, e.g. DreamZero, MolmoAct2.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jVqvJFBRcd0>

\[1x speed, autonomous\]

DSL is building the fastest cloud inference platform for robotics. We let you deploy physical AI without needing expensive local GPUs.

Robot foundation models are growing more and more computationally expensive. The latest frontier of robotics no longer fits feasibly on local GPUs. Compute costs keep soaring amidst a global LPDDR shortage; NVIDIA just doubled the prices of Jetsons in July.

**We're taking a contrarian bet that the future is moving inference _off the robot_ and _into the cloud._**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115448&key=user_uploads/3499827/4ca20fc9-00a8-4043-bc43-d51b8b5d0cbf)

How do we do this? We work across the full stack of robot inference to push latency down:

* Model-level architectural adjustments for faster inference
* Kernel-level optimizations to maximally leverage server-grade GPUs
* Network-level optimizations for fast and reliable transport over the cloud
* Region-specific compute allocation to ensure the shortest physical distance between the servers and our customers' robots

These optimizations enable us to be **8% faster** than NVIDIA's implementation **at half the GPU count** (320ms vs 350ms, for DreamZero 14B).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115448&key=user_uploads/3499827/69393040-ca17-41cd-a1fb-cd5d70176921)

Furthermore, something we noticed for robotics companies with fast R&D cycles was that their GPUs had long idle periods with concentrated bursts of inference traffic. We're one of the first companies in the world to offer on-demand pricing for physical AI inference, giving users more flexibility with the cost.

We're already working closely with a range of early partners across deployment, research and evaluation. In full FDE spirit, we collaborate with our customers to custom-fit inference stacks that address their unique deployment challenges. We help you get your robot AI to deployment faster.

Our mission is to democratize access to frontier physical intelligence, and we believe cloud is the way forward. You can read our thesis here:

•⁠ ⁠<http://dreamscalelabs.com/blog/why>

\
